source.title: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders: Leveraging the Sequential Nature of Language for Interpretability
source.authors: Usha Bhalla; Alexander X. Oesterling; C. M. Verdun; Himabindu Lakkaraju; F. Calmon

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some chart results are only shown as plots, without extractable values.
record.tranche_reason: The study probes features recovered from LLM activations by sparse autoencoders, providing indirect evidence about SAE-recoverable features in real models. It does not test superposition geometry or feature capacity directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports probing results for SAE decompositions and explicit ablation differences in semantic, contextual, and syntactic probe accuracy; these bear on V4. It does not experimentally test toy-model superposition, capacity-based polysemanticity, canonicality of SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Steering results concern deliberately induced behavior and are not evidence for those claims. Baseline comparisons and the probes are included in the main probing rows; plot-only accuracy values are not estimated.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It trains a new SAE variant (Temporal SAE) and compares its probe accuracy, smoothness, reconstruction and steering against other SAEs (Matryoshka, BatchTopK). It assumes SAE features are meaningful units and reports only its own method's performance. It does not test whether LLMs contain superposed sparse features (V4); it only tests which SAE objective yields more semantic or contextual features. Probe accuracy of one SAE versus another does not bear on whether superposition or recoverable sparse features exist. No toy models, capacity, polysemanticity causes, canonicality or feature dimensionality are measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a temporal contrastive loss lets SAEs separate semantic from syntactic features self-supervised, giving smoother, more semantically structured features with minimal reconstruction loss. They also claim practical benefits in dataset analysis (HH-RLHF spurious length features) and steering, where they say T-SAEs Pareto-dominate baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Temporal Sparse Autoencoders with a temporal contrastive objective and evaluates SAE feature probes; it does not reproduce the toy-network method or geometry of Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe outcomes vary with feature split and temporal-loss design. The authors report that increasing the high-level split improves semantic and contextual recovery but reduces syntax performance; random-past-token contrast changes context and syntax performance; removing the contrastive term reduces semantic and contextual probing performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing the SAE training prior (temporal contrastive loss, feature split ratio, contrast partner) shifts which kinds of features the dictionary recovers (semantic/contextual vs syntactic). FVE and other core metrics stay nearly unchanged (Table 1: Gemma FVE 0.75–0.76; Table 2 FVE deltas within ±0.01).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which features an SAE recovers depends on its training objective and priors, at near-equal reconstruction. This is related to V5 (non-canonicality of SAE features), but the study frames it as method design, not a canonicality test.

record.problems: The main probing accuracy values are presented in plots without transcribed numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The labels are proxies: MMLU question categories for semantics, question IDs for context, and spaCy part-of-speech tags for syntax. The paper notes that automated feature-explanation generation and judging are noisy and judge-dependent.
record.rows_left_out: Individual plotted sparsity points and separate baseline-model, Matryoshka SAE, and BatchTopK SAE curves are not separately extracted; the main probing rows describe the reported MMLU curves and textual comparisons. Additional probing curves for Wikipedia and FineFineWeb in Appendix C.5 are not included because their values are plot-only and the paper states the same trends. Table 2 probing deltas are included separately.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V4 'supports' labels are reversed here. Every row compares the study's own method with other SAEs or ablates its own objective, which the rules exclude as T4. The rows say nothing about whether LLMs contain superposed or SAE-recoverable sparse features, only which SAE recovers more semantic-label information. Steering and the case study are method utility. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
It does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.

The study tests whether SAE decompositions support probes for linguistic information in selected LLMs; it does not measure how many neurons jointly represent a feature or establish that the recovered features are the model's underlying units.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units across training runs or methods.
It does not measure whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional subspaces.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2b (Temporal SAE)
rows.operation_detail: Probe SAE activations for semantic labels.
rows.baseline: Baseline model latents, Matryoshka SAE, and BatchTopK SAE are shown as comparisons; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors state that Temporal SAE probes significantly outperform baseline SAEs on semantic labels. The plot shows multiple sparsity settings; exact points are not transcribed.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (T-SAE) with baseline SAEs on probe accuracy for semantic labels. This is a method comparison, not a measure of sparse-feature recoverability. 'Observed' has no version effect to refer to.
